name: Cortisol rhythm
goal: High cortisol after waking (strong cortisol awakening response), low cortisol before sleep.

phases.goal: Maximize cortisol: support the awakening peak

rules.title: Wake at the same time
rules.label: Wake up
rules.why: The cortisol awakening response is triggered by the act of waking; a stable wake time keeps the daily cortisol curve anchored.
rules.advice: Get up at your planned wake time, weekends included.

rules.title: Bright light soon after waking
rules.label: Get daylight
rules.why: Moving from dim to bright light in the morning produces an immediate cortisol rise; dawn light enhances the awakening response.
rules.advice: Get 10+ minutes of outdoor daylight (or bright light) within an hour of waking.

nudge.text: Step outside or into bright light for 10+ minutes in the next hour — it boosts your morning cortisol peak.

rules.title: Move in the morning
rules.label: Move
rules.why: Exercise acutely raises cortisol; placing it in the morning works with the natural peak instead of against the evening decline.
rules.advice: Fit in a walk or workout before mid-morning.

nudge.text: A short walk or workout in the next 90 minutes keeps your energy curve front-loaded.

rules.title: No caffeine within 6 h of bed
rules.label: Caffeine cut-off
rules.why: Caffeine raises cortisol and, even 6 hours before bed, measurably disrupts sleep.
rules.advice: Switch to decaf or herbal tea from now on.

nudge.text: Caffeine cut-off in 30 minutes. Last coffee now, if you want one.

rules.title: No intense exercise in the last hour
rules.label: No hard workouts
rules.why: Evening exercise is fine in general, but vigorous exercise within ~1 hour of bedtime impairs sleep onset.
rules.advice: Keep it to light stretching this close to bed.

rules.title: Dim light and screens before bed
rules.label: Dim lights & screens
rules.why: Evening light suppresses melatonin and delays the circadian clock, shifting the whole hormonal rhythm later.
rules.advice: Dim the lights, use night mode, put the phone away.

nudge.text: Two hours to bedtime: dim the lights and switch screens to night mode.

rules.title: Wind-down routine
rules.label: Wind down
rules.why: Relaxation and mindfulness practices lower cortisol.
rules.advice: 15 minutes of reading, breathing or stretching in dim light.

nudge.text: Time to wind down: 15 minutes of reading or slow breathing, lights low.

rules.title: Go to bed at the same time
rules.label: Lights out
rules.why: Short or shifted sleep raises cortisol the following evening, flattening the rhythm.
rules.advice: Lights out at your planned bedtime.
